extracted.intended_audience: researchers and proposal teams at U.S. institutions of higher education preparing Multidisciplinary University Research Initiatives (MURI) proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of Multidisciplinary University Research Initiatives (MURI) full proposals to the Office of Naval Research, addressing specified DoD research topics via multidisciplinary university-led teams. Includes eligibility, team composition, topic alignment, expected project duration/funding, and transition/impact expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multidisciplinary approach / team composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Multidisciplinary University Initiative (MURI) efforts involve teams of researchers investigating high priority topics and opportunities that intersect more than one traditional technical discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should form teams whose expertise spans multiple science and engineering fields; multidisciplinary approaches are intended to stimulate innovations, accelerate progress, and expedite transition into naval applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with specified research topics
rubrics_metrics.description: MURI awards are made in research topics specified by the participating defense agencies each year that the program is in force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must address the topics described in the current MURI funding announcement; specified topics change yearly, so proposers must ensure their work directly addresses the current announcement topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to DoD research needs / naval applications
rubrics_metrics.description: The announcement explains the DoD's research needs upon which the topics are based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should demonstrate clear relevance to DoD research needs and how outcomes will apply to naval applications (transition potential to defense use is a central expectation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Promotion of defense application and dual-use potential
rubrics_metrics.description: The DoD expects that MURI programs will promote application of defense research, principally for defense purposes but also for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should highlight how research results will be applied for defense purposes and, where appropriate, articulate commercial/dual-use potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged interactions with transition organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Interactions with research and development organizations that transition research findings to application, particularly industrial organizations, DoD laboratories, and other organizations that perform research and development for defense applications, are encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should describe planned engagement or partnerships with industry, DoD labs, or other transition-focused organizations to facilitate moving results toward application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — institutional and submission constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may be submitted only by U. S. institutions of higher education (i.e. universities) with degree granting programs in science or engineering, or by consortia of such institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the submitting organization meets the U.S. higher education and degree-granting requirement; consortia are allowed but one academic institution must be designated as the primary awardee for award execution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consortia rationale / complementary strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals from consortia of academic institutions may be warranted because research in the multidisciplinary topics may require forming teams with strengths in multiple science and engineering fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If proposing as a consortium, clearly justify the need for multiple institutions and describe complementary technical strengths and coordination mechanisms across partners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary awardee institution requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: One academic institution will be the primary awardee for purposes of award execution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a single lead institution responsible for award administration and explain institutional roles and responsibilities in consortium proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project period expectations (duration/options)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are typically for a period of three years (funded incrementally or as options) with two additional years possible as options to bring the total award to five-years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be scoped and budgeted consistent with the typical 3-year period and possible 2-year options; plan milestones and deliverables accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding level guidance / budget realism
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are at a funding level ranging from half a million to about a million dollars per year, with the size of the award dependent upon the topic, technical goals, and availability of appropriations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget requests should be justified relative to the topic and technical goals and fall within the typical annual award range; be mindful that actual funding depends on appropriations and topic priority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline / timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Full proposals will be accepted until Friday, September 6, 2024 at 5:00 PM Eastern Daylight Time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals must be submitted by the announced deadline; proposers are advised to read the full funding announcement for submission procedures and any system-specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competitive evaluation; refer to program announcement for criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated competitively. Evaluation criteria are cited in the program announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit evaluation criteria (e.g., significance, approach, investigators, etc.) are provided in the MURI funding announcement — proposers must consult that announcement for the detailed review criteria and address them in the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic specificity and annual change
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit proposals based on prior years' topics; ensure the proposed research is targeted to the current year's specific research topics described in the announcement.
